name: Slovenian nationalism
summary: Slovenian nationalism holds that Slovenes are a distinct nation with the right to their own sovereign state, language and culture, a cause that ran from the 19th-century national awakening to independence in 1991. Today it is carried mainly by national-conservative and national-populist parties, the SDS and the smaller SNS, which stress sovereignty, patriotic education, restricted immigration and suspicion of minority claims such as those of the Erased, while differing on the EU, the Church and economics.
scope: The mainstream strand from the 1989 May Declaration and 1991 independence through today's national-conservative right (Slovenian Democratic Party, Slovenian National Party). It does not model the wartime Home Guard, and it treats economics, the EU and church-state relations as areas where adherents differ, since the SDS is pro-market and church-backed while the SNS is anticlerical and Eurosceptic. Sources are mostly encyclopedic and party-descriptive, so many answers are inferred and marked low.

keyFigures.name: Anton Korošec
keyFigures.role: Early 20th-century Slovene nationalist politician whose 1917 declaration gave the May Declaration its name.

keyFigures.name: Janez Janša
keyFigures.role: Leader of the national-conservative SDS who uses the slogan Slovenia first.

universal-healthcare.rationale: The constitution guarantees a right to healthcare under legal conditions and a social state, but nationalism itself has no healthcare doctrine; SDS governments mixed pension and benefit increases with austerity.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: The SNS has backed higher minimum wages as part of its populist economics, but this is not a core nationalist position and the market-leaning SDS does not stress it.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The SDS is described as broadly pro-market while the SNS opposes mass privatisation and wants state ownership of strategic sectors, so the nationalist camp points both ways.

public-ownership.rationale: The SNS supports state ownership in strategic sectors, while the SDS favours faster privatisation; the pull toward national control of key industries makes mild agreement the likelier answer.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The SDS favours lower taxes and the SNS is economically populist, so there is no common nationalist line on taxing the wealthy.

unions-good.rationale: Nationalism has no labour doctrine, and neither the SDS nor the SNS makes unions a theme; the answer is inferred from an economically mixed camp.

property-fundamental.rationale: The constitution guarantees private property while allowing expropriation in the public interest; the national-conservative camp is property-respecting but this is not a nationalist tenet.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The SNS is populist and wary of big business while the SDS is pro-market and deregulatory; no shared nationalist position exists.

cut-welfare.rationale: The SDS cut pensions and transfers in 2012 but later agreed pension rises and a child benefit, and the SNS is populist, so adherents lean against deep welfare cuts as a nationalist stance.

worker-ownership.rationale: Cooperative ownership is not part of Slovenian nationalist thought; the camp favours either state or private ownership, so disagreement is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: National-conservative parties like the SDS favour security measures, but no source states a position on surveillance, so this is inferred from their security emphasis.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Social conservatism of the SDS and SNS suggests opposition to drug legalisation, but no source states it.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The SDS has been accused of hostile rhetoric toward minorities and opposes what it sees as leftist speech control, so adherents lean against hate-speech restrictions; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: The SDS under Janša is criticised for pressuring media and institutions, but the constitution sets separated powers and nationalists generally defend their parliamentary state.

state-harmful.rationale: Slovenian nationalism's central aim was a sovereign state of the Slovene nation, so adherents flatly reject the idea that the state is harmful.

limit-guns.rationale: The SDS supports loosening civilian firearm controls and Janša urged citizens to arm themselves in 2023.

empower-police-military.rationale: The SDS backs mandatory military service and proposed a 25,000-strong national guard, pointing to strengthened security forces.

decide-locally.rationale: The constitution makes the state territorially indivisible and nationalists stress national sovereignty, though it also guarantees local self-government (Art. 9); inferred as a mild lean to the nation level.

rehabilitation.rationale: No nationalist source addresses penal philosophy; conservative camps lean punitive but rehabilitation is also official policy.

traditional-family.rationale: The SDS and SNS are socially conservative and the SDS opposes same-sex marriage, matching a family-centred view of society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The SDS opposes same-sex marriage despite introducing civil unions in government, and the SNS opposes expanded rights for sexual minorities.

abortion-legal.rationale: No source documents a nationalist position; the Catholic-aligned SDS and the anticlerical SNS plausibly differ, so adherents are mixed.

more-religion-public.rationale: The Church backs the SDS, but the SNS is strongly anticlerical and the constitution separates church and state, so the nationalist camp has no common view.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a Slovenian nationalist issue; the camp's hostility to minority claims, notably Roma and the Erased, suggests disagreement.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Social conservatism and opposition to expanded rights for sexual minorities suggest rejecting the claim, but no source speaks to it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Slovenian nationalism is defined as promoting the cultural unity of Slovenes, and the 1989 May Declaration asserts the Slovene nation's own state.

gradual-change.rationale: National conservatives value continuity, yet Slovenian nationalism's founding act was a rapid break from Yugoslavia, so the answer is mixed.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The SDS is strongly anti-immigration and opposes EU migrant quotas, and the SNS is critical of immigration and multiculturalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The SNS is hard Eurosceptic and opposes transferring sovereignty to supranational bodies, and nationalism prioritises national self-rule.

free-trade.rationale: The SDS is pro-market while the SNS is economically populist, and nationalism has no fixed trade doctrine.

nation-first.rationale: Janša has used the phrase Slovenia first and the SNS resists supranational integration, though the SDS also stays in NATO and the EU.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Neither party documents a stance; the SNS opposes NATO while the SDS supports it.

open-borders.rationale: With strongly anti-immigration parties and a constitutional state built around a national community, open borders are far outside this camp.

limit-growth.rationale: The national-conservative camp is pro-growth, but no source addresses degrowth; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No documented nationalist position; the SDS's right-of-centre economics suggest scepticism of drastic government action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Nationalism has no stance on technological optimism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Slovenia operates the Krško plant and a national-conservative energy-security outlook favours it, but no source gives a party position.

revolution-justified.rationale: Slovenia's independence came through a democratic plebiscite and constitutional process, and the May Declaration tied statehood to democracy and human rights.

experts-over-public.rationale: The SDS rhetorically opposes elites and says media and academia are leftist-controlled, so adherents distrust expert rule; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Even the state-ownership-minded SNS wants a market economy with strategic public holdings, and the SDS is neoliberal.

socialized-markets.rationale: The SNS likes state control of strategic sectors but no source speaks to worker or public ownership as a market condition.

land-value-tax.rationale: A niche proposal outside Slovenian nationalism, and the SDS favours lower taxes by other means; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The SDS favours lower taxes and the family-centred right typically opposes heavy inheritance taxes; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Not a nationalist theme and the SDS is welfare-cautious; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The SNS resists privatisation and foreign control but EU membership rules out national tariffs, and no source states a view.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The SNS favours state ownership in strategic sectors while the SDS is market-leaning.

widespread-small-property.rationale: No source documents a position on distributive property ownership.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Both major nationalist parties work within a market economy with money and wages.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Slovenia's nationalists campaigned for sovereignty, not monetary anarchism, and the SDS is a mainstream party; no support for this.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: No documented support for state-recognised wage and price bodies; inferred from the camp's market lean.

one-party-rule.rationale: The May Declaration grounded statehood in democracy with political pluralism, and the nationalist movement arose against the one-party Yugoslav system.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Slovenia is a republic and no mainstream nationalist current seeks a monarch, though some historic figures were monarchist; inferred.

democracy-best.rationale: The founding documents tie the Slovene state to democracy and pluralism, though no source speaks to the phrase even when voters choose badly.

direct-votes.rationale: Slovenian nationalists have used referendums, including the 1990 independence plebiscite and a push for an immigration referendum, but no source states a general rule.

workers-councils.rationale: The nationalist movement was a pluralist, anti-communist reaction to Yugoslav socialist self-management and favours parliamentary democracy.

right-to-secede.rationale: Slovenia's own independence rested on the Slovene nation's right of secession from Yugoslavia, though adherents resist dividing Slovenia itself.

natural-rulers.rationale: The May Declaration frames power in democratic terms; no source supports innate ruling classes.

political-violence-never.rationale: Nationalists defend the 1991 independence defence, while the Home Guard legacy remains disputed, so adherents differ.

war-builds-character.rationale: No source documents a glorification of war; Slovene nationalism is largely a cultural and constitutional movement.

separate-church-state.rationale: The constitution separates church and state and the SNS is strongly anticlerical, but the SDS is backed by the Church, so adherents split on strictness.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitution separates religious communities from the state and no mainstream Slovenian nationalist current seeks scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Nationalists see the state as the guarantor of the nation, and the SDS backs a national army and guard.

military-superiority.rationale: Slovenia is a small NATO state and no source documents ambitions for military superiority.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Slovenian nationalism centres on the Slovene nation, though the constitution calls Slovenia a state of all its citizens and protects Italian and Hungarian communities.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Slovenian nationalism treats nations, not classes, as the unit of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: No documented position; the market-leaning right rejects equality of outcomes, though the SNS is economically populist.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Slovenia has no indigenous-lands issue; the constitution protects autochthonous Italian and Hungarian communities but without land authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not a Slovenian issue; right-leaning nationalists generally oppose reparations claims.

civilizational-union.rationale: The SNS is hard Eurosceptic and Slovenian nationalism emphasises the Slovene nation rather than supranational unions.

duties-before-rights.rationale: National-conservative rhetoric stresses patriotic duty, but the Slovene constitutional order is rights-based.

limit-population.rationale: The SDS-side stresses family and demographic renewal, so adherents oppose limiting population; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Slovenian nationalism is not anti-industrial and the main nationalist parties are pro-growth.

human-enhancement.rationale: Socially conservative parties are likely wary; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: No documented position; national-conservatives favour human political accountability.

restore-past-order.rationale: National conservatives value tradition but the nationalist project is forward-looking statehood, so no unified answer.

direct-action.rationale: Statehood was pursued through party politics and a plebiscite, with the May Declaration emerging from a rally but leading to elections.

return-to-foraging.rationale: No Slovenian nationalist source or party endorses primitivism.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not part of any Slovenian nationalist programme.

distribute-by-need.rationale: A communist ideal that the nationalist camp, defined partly against Yugoslav socialism, does not share.

production-for-use.rationale: Not a nationalist position and the nationalist camp accepts market production.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Marxist labour theory is foreign to Slovenian nationalism, and the SDS is pro-market.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The May Declaration demanded pluralist democracy against the one-party Yugoslav socialist order, which makes proletarian dictatorship opposed to the movement's founding aims.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivisation is associated with Yugoslav communism, which Slovene nationalists rejected.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: A Marxist thesis outside nationalist thought.

taxation-theft.rationale: The SDS favours lower taxes but still governs through a taxing state.

harm-principle.rationale: No documented position; social conservatism restricts private conduct on moral grounds.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The constitution protects group rights of Italian and Hungarian minorities, and nationalism centres on a collective, the nation.

conscription.rationale: The SDS supports reinstating mandatory military service of at least six months, and the constitution makes national defence participation compulsory.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Nationalism values civic participation in a sovereign state over exit; inferred.

state-as-business.rationale: The SDS is market-leaning but nationalism treats the state as the nation's instrument, not a firm.

positive-liberty.rationale: The constitution describes a social state, but no nationalist source discusses this philosophical claim.

media-academia-power.rationale: The SDS says the media is controlled by leftist groups and runs its own outlet, Nova24TV.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Slovenian nationalism is cultural and linguistic, and no source documents racial theories.

organic-representation.rationale: No source supports corporate representation; nationalists operate through parties.

total-state.rationale: The nationalist movement emerged against a one-party state and demanded pluralism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Independence is framed as a national awakening, but no source documents a call for radical rebirth from decadence.

territorial-expansion.rationale: The constitution frames a territorially unified existing state, and no mainstream party advocates expansion.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal oaths of loyalty are incompatible with the democratic republic the nationalist movement built.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is far outside Slovenian nationalism and the constitution guarantees freedom of labour.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Postmodern epistemology is not nationalist, and the SDS-side distrusts what it calls leftist academia.

universal-morality.rationale: Catholic-aligned conservatism leans yes, but the nationalist camp is not unified on this.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: No documented position in Slovenian nationalism; SDS governments have been friendly to Israel while the SNS has no stated line.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The constitution allows special rights, by law, for Slovenes without citizenship and commits to concern for Slovenes abroad.

revive-national-language.rationale: Slovene never fell out of everyday use, so the question is mostly moot even though language is central to the movement.

workplace-democracy.rationale: A socialist-self-management idea associated with Yugoslavia rather than nationalism.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The SDS imposed an austerity package in 2012, suggesting fiscal caution.

economic-freedom.rationale: The SDS leans neoliberal, but the SNS differs and no source frames freedom as a nationalist tenet.

rule-by-example.rationale: No documented position and Slovenia is a constitutional republic.

national-self-determination.rationale: The May Declaration expressly asserts the people's wish to live in a sovereign state of the Slovene nation, and the constitution grounds itself on the nation's right to self-determination.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The SDS draws Church backing, but the anticlerical SNS differs; no source states a view.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Anti-immigration parties like the SDS and SNS favour limiting benefits to the national community, consistent with their opposition to immigration.

work-for-welfare.rationale: A conservative lean, but no source states the SDS or SNS position directly.

class-collaboration.rationale: Nationalism treats the nation as the unit of solidarity above class conflict.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Preserving national cultural heritage is central to Slovene nationalism.

dominated-front.rationale: Slovenia is Western-aligned and the SDS supports NATO, so a front against the West is outside the camp.

workers-nation.rationale: Slovenian nationalism puts the national community before an international working class.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Social conservatism leans yes but Slovene law is equality-based and no source documents it.

ban-interest.rationale: No Slovenian nationalist source supports banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: The constitution guarantees equal rights and protects minorities, and no mainstream Slovenian nationalist movement proposes segregation.

state-class-instrument.rationale: A Marxist claim that nationalism rejects, since the state represents the nation.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Anti-immigration and anti-multiculturalist parties lean toward expecting immigrants to join the national culture, though no source states it precisely.

elite-replacement.rationale: The SDS has links to Identitarian circles and published a book from the alt-right, but mainstream adherents are not all in agreement.

proportional-representation.rationale: Slovenia uses proportional representation and the nationalist parties compete in it, but no source records a party position.

national-mission.rationale: Slovene nationalism concerns a small nation's own state, not exporting its system.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Social conservatives typically reject the claim; no source states it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Janša's SDS campaigns against political and media elites as leftist networks, and the SNS has a populist character.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics runs against constitutional rights and is not part of Slovenian nationalism.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The SDS defends the independence-war security forces and rejects postwar communist reckoning only in one direction; no source states a position.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The constitution makes Slovenia a social state and the SNS favours state ownership, so a minimal state is not the nationalist line.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Slovenian nationalism is defined by language and culture, and the constitution guarantees equality; no source supports it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The constitution and May Declaration commit to human rights and equal protection, although critics note hostility to some minorities.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist debate with no connection to Slovenian nationalism.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Not a Slovenian issue; right-nationalists tend to reject colonial framings of states.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The constitution makes Slovenia a state of all its citizens with state-religion separation, so a single civil law is consistent.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The constitution guarantees religious equality and separation of church and state.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: An Indian issue with no connection to Slovenian nationalism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: The constitution separates church and state, but the SDS enjoys Church backing, so adherents differ.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Soviet-era doctrine opposed to the pluralist democracy Slovene nationalists sought.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The May Declaration ties the Slovene state to democracy and rests the nation's sovereignty on its own will, the view that legitimacy comes from the governed.

population-transfer.rationale: The constitution protects minorities and the Erased dispute was about residency rights, not expulsion.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Some nationalist writing frames nations in struggle, but no Slovenian source documents it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: No documented position; Slovenian right-wingers resist banning parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Independence from Yugoslav domination fits the idea, but no source states the republican theory.

separated-powers.rationale: The constitution sets separation of legislative, executive and judicial power, which the republic's nationalists operate within, though the SDS has been criticised on media pressure.

vanguard-party.rationale: The nationalist movement arose against a vanguard-party state.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The SNS is populist but no source documents this principle.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: The market-leaning SDS may favour restrictions, but no source states it.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: No documented position; the nationalist camp promotes higher birthrates.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Opposition to multiculturalism and immigration by the SNS and SDS is built on cohesion and identity concerns.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: No source supports sortition; the republic uses elections.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The SDS is accused of aggressive pandemic-era measures and press pressure, yet it has no documented doctrine.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: The SNS is populist, but no source states a view.

party-controls-media.rationale: The founding demand for pluralist democracy rules out party media control.

party-commands-army.rationale: Slovenian nationalism built a national, constitutional army and rejected party-commanded forces.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Hard-line immigration and Erased-related stances suggest preferring strict naturalisation, but no source gives a period.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: A populist idea; no source documents it.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: The SNS is hard Eurosceptic while the SDS is pro-European, so adherents differ.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Slovene president commands the armed forces but the government chooses ministers; no nationalist source states a view.

clerical-rule.rationale: Slovenia separates church and state and no nationalist current wants clerical rule.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist doctrine that nationalism opposes.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Social conservatism may support some censorship but no source documents it.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: No source records nationalist parties seeking unlimited presidential terms in the republic they operate within; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The SDS wants to stay in NATO, though the SNS has called for withdrawal or a redefined role.

people-in-arms.rationale: The SDS has proposed a volunteer national guard and arming of citizens, but a full replacement of the army is not a stated aim.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Romantic nationalism often values rural tradition, but no Slovenian source documents it.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The SDS attacks academia as leftist, but no source states the claim directly.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Slovenes live as minorities in Italy, Austria and Hungary and the constitution commits to concern for them, but no source states a call for reunification.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Opposition to multiculturalism implies rejecting cultural equivalence, but no source states it.

death-penalty.rationale: Slovenia has abolished capital punishment and no source records nationalist parties seeking its return; a mild lean against is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Social conservatism of the main nationalist parties suggests opposition, but no source documents a position.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: The SDS opposes expanded rights for sexual minorities and promotes patriotic education, suggesting resistance to gender-equality curricula; no source states it.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The constitution separates church and state, and no Slovene nationalist source seeks creationism in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Social conservatives lean yes while liberal currents in the camp lean no, and no source documents a position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: The constitution lets the state grant special rights to Slovenes without citizenship and nationalism defines the nation by Slovene identity, favouring descent; the Erased dispute shows reluctance to grant citizenship by residence.

minority-language-support.rationale: The constitution makes Italian and Hungarian official in the municipalities where those communities live, a policy Slovene nationalism has accepted as part of the national settlement.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Nationalists who criticise multiculturalism are unlikely to favour exemptions for religious minorities; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: A conformity-valuing national-conservative outlook suggests disagreement, but no source states it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: No documented position; the SDS's fiscal caution suggests debts should be repaid.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: The May Declaration paired sovereignty with democracy and a prosperous society, not a transformed property system.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Slovenia adopted its constitution in 1991 through its elected assembly, but no source records a position on rewriting it.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The nationalist movement demanded human rights and political pluralism as the base of the Slovene state.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The nation-first, anti-immigration camp is unlikely to push for large foreign aid; inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Slovenia is a small state and the SDS supports NATO membership and collective defence, not its own nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Slovenia's president is directly elected and the nationalist camp accepts this, though no source gives a party position.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The SNS is sovereigntist and Eurosceptic while the SDS is pro-European, so views on the independent ECB differ.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: The constitution makes the state territorially indivisible, which suggests resisting land concessions, but no source applies this to peace deals.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The constitution says property serves economic, social and environmental functions, but nationalists differ over how far that limits owners.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A leftist debate with no stated nationalist position; the camp sees Yugoslav and Soviet socialism as one failed order.

precautionary-principle.rationale: No documented position; right-leaning economics suggest scepticism of anticipatory regulation.

collective-defense.rationale: The SDS is committed to continued NATO membership, though the SNS opposed accession and has called for withdrawal.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Slovenian nationalism rests on a view of sovereignty needing the people's consent, but no source addresses annexation specifically.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The SNS is strongly anticlerical while the Church backs the SDS, so the camp is divided.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The president is meant to represent the state above parties, but no nationalist source states this view.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Slovenia itself seceded from Yugoslavia, which makes adherents unlikely to endorse force against secession in principle; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The constitution guarantees local self-government but no nationalist source discusses autonomy within a larger state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Slovenia is a republic and no nationalist source supports a sacred ruler.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The SDS favours lower taxes but no source records a flat-tax position.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The constitution makes Slovenia a state governed by the rule of law, which nationalists operate within.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No documented position; the republic has separated powers and a bicameral-style structure but no source ties it to nationalism.

leader-cult.rationale: The SDS and Janša attract devoted followings but no source documents leader worship, and Slovenian political culture is wary of it after Yugoslav Tito cult.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist thesis alien to Slovenian nationalism.

land-redistribution.rationale: No documented position; Slovenian nationalists are generally property-protective and anti-communist.

refugee-return.rationale: Slovenian nationalist parties are restrictive on migrants and refugees, with the SDS opposing EU migrant quotas.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The constitution commits to concern for Slovenes abroad and to special rights, but frames the state within its existing territory, and no mainstream party claims foreign land.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The constitution guarantees religious equality and separates church and state.

women-must-cover.rationale: Not part of Slovenian nationalism, though nationalists critical of Islam might favour covering bans, not mandates.

common-currency.rationale: Slovenia uses the euro; the SDS is pro-European but the SNS is hard Eurosceptic.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Slovene nationalism turned from the Yugoslav South Slavic union toward independence, as the May Declaration shows.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The constitution grants Italian and Hungarian communities special rights, but no source records nationalists' view of this model for other minorities.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Slovenian nationalism holds that nations and culture, not economic structure, drive history.

ban-cartels.rationale: The SNS populist critique of concentrated interests suggests agreement, but no source states it.

no-bailouts.rationale: The SDS is market-leaning but its record includes austerity, and no source states a bailout position.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The SDS has clashed with courts and media, but the constitution ties the state to rule of law, and no source states the principle.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Social conservatives typically oppose quotas; no source states it.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Slovenia is a small open EU economy and no nationalist source advocates autarky.

moral-incentives.rationale: Not part of any Slovenian nationalist programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Slovenian nationalism pursued independence through plebiscite and state institutions, not revolutionary vanguardism.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Slovenia is a republic with no titled order and nationalists accept this; no source states a position.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The SDS advocates patriotic education from kindergarten to high school, and nationalism centres on the Slovene national story.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Slovene nationalism arose against foreign rule over a small nation and does not endorse tutelage of others.

patriotic-education.rationale: The SDS explicitly advocates patriotic education from kindergarten through high school.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Race-based admissions are not a Slovenian question, but the right-leaning camp would likely oppose such preferences.

public-money-creation.rationale: No documented position; the SDS-side is conventional on monetary matters.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Slovenia was part of Austria and Yugoslavia, and nationalism defines itself against both, with no stated policy of cultivating influence.

delink-world-market.rationale: Slovenia is a small open economy and neither major nationalist party advocates delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist concept foreign to Slovenian nationalism.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Nationalist parties accused of hostility to minorities may defend private discrimination in practice, but no source states it, and Slovene law is anti-discrimination.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The constitution has an entrenched rights chapter and the independence movement was tied to human rights, but no source states a general position.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: No documented position; Slovenian history is of imperial rule, not colonial treaties.

elective-rulers.rationale: The republican, democratic state demanded in the May Declaration implies chosen rulers.

minority-veto.rationale: The constitution gives Italian and Hungarian minorities representation but not a general veto.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Slovenia is a parliamentary republic and the nationalist parties operate through parliament, but no source states parliamentary supremacy.

animal-use-humane.rationale: A conventional conservative view, but no source states it.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Slovenian nationalism is an activist political movement and its history, from the May Declaration rally onward, is of public engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: A Frankfurt School claim; nationalist parties blame leftist media instead, so partial overlap only.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian idea; no source states it, though the SDS claims leftists dominate culture and media.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim with little traction in Slovenia, which is a developed economy.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anti-immigration parties would lean toward restricting office to the native-born, but no source states it.

party-own-road.rationale: The Slovene communists' own road within Yugoslavia is not a nationalist theme, but the movement stresses decision-making independence of Slovenia, so mild agreement is inferred.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Slovenia's neighbours' territorial disputes with Croatia exist but no source documents Slovenian nationalist demands for lost lands.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not a Slovenian issue; the constitution treats all citizens equally.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: The SDS has been criticised over World War II memory and the SNS over its views on postwar history, so adherents disagree sharply.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The SDS-side stresses communist crimes alongside fascist ones, and criticism of the SNS concerns its views of WWII history.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US issue; no Slovene nationalist position.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: No documented position; Slovenia's own monument fights involve both communist and Home Guard memory.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Social conservatives often favour this, but no source states it.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The constitution places the army under civilian authority and Slovenian nationalism operates within the republic.

paid-care-work.rationale: No documented position, though the SDS child benefit points to family support.

filial-duty.rationale: Family-centred conservative values suggest agreement, but no source states it.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: The SNS opposes mass privatisation and wants strategic sectors in domestic hands, which implies blocking foreign takeover.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Conservative and Catholic-aligned leaning against, but no source records a position.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The constitution uses representative democracy and no source records support for binding mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The SDS cut pensions and is market-leaning but later raised them, with no stated stance on private accounts.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The constitution guarantees private property and inheritance, and Slovenian nationalism is not communitarian on land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Slovenia is a parliamentary republic under rule of law and no nationalist source argues otherwise.

single-official-language.rationale: Slovene is the sole state language but the constitution also gives Italian and Hungarian official status locally, and nationalists accept both.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: The SNS is protective of national resources, but Slovenia as an EU member must allow EU citizens to buy land and no source records a nationalist demand.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: A US-style civil-rights doctrine; no source records support, and right-leaning nationalists typically reject outcome-based discrimination tests.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Slovenia is a small state and no nationalist source supports arming insurgents abroad.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Slovenian nationalism arose from resisting Yugoslav federal military pressure on Slovenia's own sovereignty, which opposes the doctrine of intervening to stop an ally leaving.

corporate-influence.rationale: The SNS has populist anti-elite rhetoric that would extend to lobbying, but no source states it.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The SDS has proposed moving money from NGOs to security spending and is hostile to leftist NGOs, in line with restricting foreign funding for sovereignty reasons.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: The SDS stresses family policy and a universal child benefit, and nationalism links demographic renewal to national survival rather than immigration.

job-guarantee.rationale: No documented position; the SDS-side is market-leaning.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Rule-of-law constitutionalism and conservative respect for order make adherents disagree; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Slovenian nationalism invoked sovereignty against Yugoslav interference, but no source states an absolute rule.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Some SDS-linked circles promote replacement narratives and the SNS has been accused of hostile views on Roma, but mainstream adherents do not state a conspiracy thesis.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: The SDS and SNS are family-centred conservatives who oppose same-sex marriage, and so defend state-recognised marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: The SDS has been criticised over media transparency, but no source documents its position.

informal-organisation.rationale: Slovene nationalism has organised through parties and national institutions.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The SNS resists transfers of sovereignty to supranational bodies, though the constitution says laws must follow international law.

religious-nation.rationale: The nation is defined by Slovene identity and language, and the constitution separates church and state, even though the Church backs the SDS.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The nationalist movement was a reaction against domination by Belgrade and Vienna before it.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The constitution guarantees private property including personal property.

defeat-communism.rationale: Slovenian nationalism emerged as a movement against the Yugoslav communist system, and SDS-side parties emphasise anti-communism.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: No documented position; the SDS is pro-market and the SNS state-leaning.

religion-illusion.rationale: The SNS is anticlerical, but Catholic-aligned parties reject this, so adherents differ.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: A socialist-feminist claim not made in nationalist sources.

socialized-care.rationale: Family-centred conservatives prefer care within families; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Slovene language protection is central, but no source documents purism as a nationalist demand.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not a Slovene issue, and the constitution says ratified treaties apply directly.

majority-settlement.rationale: The constitution protects minorities and no source documents a settlement policy.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The SNS blends left and right economics but frames this as populism, not a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Slovenian nationalism rests on a historic national territory, but no source documents it as a principle over others' claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No source ties either mainstream party to Holocaust denial.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: The SDS introduced civil unions in government and no Slovene nationalist party calls for criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The nationalist movement demanded political pluralism against a one-party state.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The constitution separates church and state and guarantees religious equality.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Slovenian nationalism arose among a small nation under foreign rule and never held colonies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Foreign to Slovenian nationalism, which is critical of Islam-related immigration.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The constitution makes the state secular and neutral between religions.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The nationalist camp favours referendums but no source states a participatory ideal.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: An academic feminist idea that right-nationalist parties reject; no source states it.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The SDS opposes expanded rights for sexual minorities and backed Hungary's child-protection limits on LGBT topics.

assisted-dying.rationale: Catholic-aligned and conservative stance suggests opposition, but no source records a position.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The SNS has been described as mixing left and right, while the SDS is clearly right, so adherents differ.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept not part of Slovenian nationalism.

islam-incompatible.rationale: The SNS is critical of immigration and multiculturalism and the SDS strongly anti-migration, but sources do not give the exact claim.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The constitution grounds power in the people, and even Church-aligned nationalists work within that order.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: The constitution separates church and state, but no source states a position on religious dress.

social-market-economy.rationale: The constitution defines Slovenia as a social state with market economy, but nationalists differ on its extent.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The SDS backs mandatory service and a national guard, and Slovenia's independence rested on its own defence forces, so abolition is rejected.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: The SDS supports continued NATO membership, though the SNS opposed accession and favours withdrawal or a redefined role, so views differ.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Slovenia is a republic and no source supports dynastic succession.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not part of any Slovenian nationalist programme.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The SDS imposed its own austerity in 2012 but populist SNS rhetoric differs, so no common view.

property-franchise.rationale: The nationalist movement demanded democratic pluralism and the constitution gives universal suffrage rights to citizens.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept that nationalism does not use.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The SDS says leftist groups control the media, partially resembling a complaint about who owns the presses, but not in the economic-class form.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: The constitution makes Slovenia a rule-of-law state, which nationalists work within, but no source states a position.

racial-franchise.rationale: The constitution makes Slovenia a state of all its citizens, and the nation is defined by culture and language.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: The constitution guarantees religious equality, and no source records support for such restriction.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: No source records Slovenian nationalist mainstream parties calling for boycotts of minority businesses.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Parties of the camp rely on parliament and referendums, and no source records support.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The SNS has a populist suspicion of concentrated power but the SDS is pro-market.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: No documented position; the SDS introduced civil unions but opposes marriage equality.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Even the anticlerical SNS wants separation of church and state, not state atheism, and the nationalist camp rejects the Yugoslav model.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The camp supports strengthened security forces.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The constitution guarantees representation for Italian and Hungarian minorities but nationalists favour a unitary national state with majority rule.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The SDS is market-leaning but passed universal child benefit, so views differ.

vote-delegation.rationale: No source records support for liquid democracy in Slovenian nationalism.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Church-aligned SDS side is allied with the Catholic Church, which restricts the priesthood; no source states a position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Slovene law has equal spouses, and no source records conservative nationalists seeking to restore husbandly authority.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Hostile to immigration and the Erased, the camp is unlikely to extend local votes to foreigners.

rent-control.rationale: The market-leaning SDS is likely to oppose rent caps, but no source states it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The SDS stresses patriotic education and national service but no source supports drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Slovenia has no nuclear weapons and no nationalist source seeks them; the SDS supports NATO membership, but no source addresses basing.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The SNS opposed NATO accession while the SDS supports membership, and no source records a view on bases.

recognise-genocide.rationale: No source records a position, but recognising historic atrocities against nations resonates with nationalist memory politics.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The SNS populism may favour this but the SDS is pro-capital.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Slovenian nationalism rests on national defence and the SDS promotes defence and arming citizens.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Slovene nationalism asserts the Slovenes as a long-lived nation whose unity predates the Napoleonic-era awakening.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Social conservatism opposes the claim; no source states it.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: A feminist theory outside nationalism, and conservatives would reject it.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Independence-war dead are honoured, but no source states a doctrine of national martyrdom.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: No documented support in Slovenian nationalism.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The constitution commits Slovenia to concern for Slovene emigrants and minorities abroad, treating the homeland as their cultural centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Slovenian nationalism culminated in statehood and the May Declaration demanded a sovereign state, not just cultural renewal.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: A feminist theology claim outside nationalism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: The SNS has resisted foreign and privatised control, but no source records a demand for majority-group economic control.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Slovenian nationalism seeks to keep the Slovene people in one state, and Slovenes in border areas are supported, but no source states the principle.

independent-unions.rationale: No source documents a position; independence from party control follows from the pluralist founding.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution describes a social state and the SNS favours public ownership of strategic sectors, so public essentials fit.

second-chamber.rationale: Slovenia has a weak second chamber, the National Council, but no source records a nationalist position.

municipal-property.rationale: The constitution guarantees private property and the nationalist camp is not municipalist.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The constitution makes the state unitary and indivisible.

family-wage.rationale: A family-centred conservative idea; no source states it.

person-over-state.rationale: The constitution is rights-based, but nationalism emphasises collective national interests.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Catholic-aligned SDS leans yes but the anticlerical SNS differs.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: The unitary constitution makes the state indivisible while guaranteeing local self-government by law.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The constitution makes Slovenia a state of all its citizens, and nationalism is organised on ethnic and linguistic, not racial, lines.

racial-pride.rationale: Slovenian nationalism is cultural and linguistic, with no source documenting racial pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Slovenia fought only a defensive independence war, and its nationalism has no expansionist programme.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Slovenian nationalism promotes the cultural unity of Slovenes, and the constitution commits to concern for Slovene minorities abroad.

communal-electorates.rationale: The constitution gives Italian and Hungarian communities guaranteed representation, but nationalism favours a general citizens' electorate otherwise.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The SNS and SDS have accused outside elites of undermining the nation but not of partition.

free-public-college.rationale: No documented position; SDS is market-leaning while SNS populist.

pollution-taxes.rationale: The SDS favours lower taxes; no source states a position.

future-generations.rationale: A conservative commonplace, but no source states it.

arms-reduction.rationale: The SDS favours stronger defence and a national guard.

capital-controls.rationale: Euro membership limits this, and no source records a stance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The SDS supports loosening civilian firearm controls and a volunteer guard, a partial departure from a state arms monopoly.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: The nationalist camp supports defence service and conscription.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: The SDS's austerity record points to fiscal caution but no source states a position on legal rules.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: A development-economics demand not held by Slovenian nationalism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Slovene nationalists built and defend a national state and operate within the constitution.

sacred-nation.rationale: Slovene nationalism celebrates the nation but is not described as sacralising it.

student-debt-relief.rationale: A US issue; right-leaning fiscal caution suggests disagreement.

internal-colonialism.rationale: The unitary state framework offers no basis for this.

shared-human-nature.rationale: A Catholic-conservative idea but no source states it.

public-service-media.rationale: The SDS has clashed with public media over alleged leftist bias, and runs its own outlet.

religions-one-truth.rationale: No documented position; Catholic-aligned adherents would likely reject it.

farm-price-support.rationale: Populist and national-protective, but no source states a position.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Slovenia has none and the issue is moot.

workers-own-party.rationale: No documented position; nationalists favour national parties not class ones.

ban-fgm.rationale: The constitution guarantees human rights and bodily integrity, and no source records adherents' opposition.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The constitution guarantees property and inheritance rights equally and no source records opposition.

one-language-many-names.rationale: A South Slavic naming issue; no source states a Slovenian nationalist position.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The constitution has no place for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: No documented position; market-leaning right lean against.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: A law-and-order lean consistent with stronger police, but no source states it.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: The Slovene language is central to the nation and nationalists oppose multiculturalism, which implies expecting immigrants to learn Slovene.

voter-id.rationale: Anti-immigration right parties often favour ID rules but no source states it for Slovenia.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: The constitution gives religious communities equal rights.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The May Declaration grounds the state in political pluralism and democratic procedure, but no source defines democracy this narrowly.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: No documented position; the SDS is accused of media pressure but not of internet shutdowns.

women-suffrage.rationale: Slovenia's constitution grants equal rights to all citizens, and no source records opposition to women voting.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The anticlerical SNS may agree but the Church-aligned SDS strongly disagrees.

homestead-ownership.rationale: A libertarian doctrine not found in Slovenian nationalism.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Eurosceptic nationalists resist supranational bodies while the SDS is pro-European.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The nationalist movement is not fundamentalist, and the constitution is secular.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The nationalist movement opposed the Yugoslav planned socialist state.

indirect-election.rationale: Slovenia directly elects its president, and the 1989 pluralist democratic demand implies direct elections.

national-church-status.rationale: The Church backs the SDS but the SNS is anticlerical and the constitution gives equal rights, so nationalists differ.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The unitary, indivisible state favours local self-government and minority rights in municipalities but not territorial autonomy.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Slovenia's own independence came through a plebiscite, a model nationalists endorse; applying to disputed territory is inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Not a Slovenian issue, though the constitution insists on indivisible territory.

equal-conscription.rationale: The SDS supports mandatory service, but no source states whether women should be included.

premarital-sex.rationale: Slovenia is a secular society and no source records nationalist parties campaigning against premarital sex, though social conservatives may disapprove.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Slovenian constitution commits the state to concern for Slovene minorities and emigrants abroad and allows special rights for Slovenes without citizenship.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from its stress on the Slovene nation's identity and sovereign homeland; the sources do not use spiritual language.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: The 1991 constitution guarantees due process and bans the death penalty, and mainstream Slovenian nationalism works within it.

close-ties-china.rationale: Inferred from the SDS and SNS support for NATO and Western ties; China is not discussed.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist right's market and property orientation; adherents differ on economics.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the constitution's human rights and the SDS's liberal stance; adherents do not use ownership language.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: The sources do not report a position, and SDS and SNS economics differ.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Adherents are split: the SNS has populist social leanings while the SDS leans market.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Its main carriers are themselves parties working through parliament, so bypassing them is not a stated aim; inferred.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the SDS's pro-market stance and anti-corruption rhetoric.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Adherents are split: the SDS is church-backed and the SNS anticlerical, while the constitution separates church and state.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Inferred from its patriotic education and cultural focus alongside membership of modern Europe.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from Slovenia's secular legal order and equal rights in the constitution; not a nationalist topic.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from its stress on sovereignty; the sources do not report a position on foreign ownership of resources.

missingStatements.text: A state should protect and support members of its nation living as minorities in neighbouring countries.
missingStatements.rationale: The Slovenian constitution commits the state to concern for Slovene minorities and emigrants abroad and allows special rights for Slovenes without citizenship.

notes: The SDS and SNS diverge sharply on economics (market-oriented versus state-ownership populism), the EU and NATO (pro versus hard Eurosceptic), and the Church (backed by versus anticlerical); those answers are mostly low or neutral. The constitution calls Slovenia a state of all its citizens, so civic and ethnic strands coexist.
